task: Ove GO for the self-hosted bypass: the org spending limit kills every GitHub-hosted job, so Quality Gates cannot run at all on ubuntu-latest. Move the gate workflows onto the org VPS self-hosted runner by changing runs-on to [self-hosted, Linux, X64] in .github/workflows/gates.yml (jobs gates, gate-self-test), .github/workflows/gates-template-sync.yml (job sync) and the distributable template ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml (jobs gates, gate-self-test). runs-on only — no gate logic, no Python version, no step body changes.

evidence.runner: Org self-hosted GitHub Actions runner, agent name srv1778002, installed at /opt/actions-runner on the SWC Studio VPS.
evidence.why: Hosted ubuntu-latest jobs fail in roughly 3 seconds with a spending-limit annotation, so no gate reaches its first step. The VPS runner is org-level and unmetered by GitHub billing.
evidence.runner_state_note: This container has no path to the VPS, so the runner's online state and its exact label set were not observed here. They come from the work order. If srv1778002 does not carry all three labels, the jobs queue instead of failing — see unverified.

claims.claim: Every runs-on in the three gate workflows is now the label set [self-hosted, Linux, X64]: gates and gate-self-test in the live workflow, sync in the template-sync workflow, and gates and gate-self-test in the distributable template. Five jobs, no ubuntu-latest left in either workflow directory.

Nothing but runs-on changed. Diffed against origin/main across .github/workflows and ci/.github/workflows, every added or removed content line is either the old ubuntu-latest line or the new self-hosted line — no gate logic, no Python version, no step body, no trigger, no permissions block moved.

The live gate workflow and its distributable template are still body-identical after the leading comment block, which is exactly the comparison the gates-template-sync job makes, so that gate stays green on this change.
The gate test suite still passes unchanged — 90 tests — so moving the runner did not disturb what the gates assert.

All three changed workflow files fall inside bot-05-infrastructure's owned paths (.github/workflows/** and ci/.github/workflows/**), so G-1 attributes this change cleanly with no foreign-path carve-out needed.
The ownership manifest still validates after this change — 7 bots, 100 rules — because this change does not touch ownership.yaml.

No credential is committed by this change. The secret scanner reports clean on all three workflow files; the runner is addressed by label, and labels are not secrets — no runner registration token, no VPS hostname, no SSH material appears in the diff.
This change performs no deployment and no destructive operation, so G-5/G-6 has nothing to gate: it edits three YAML files in the repository and touches no live system.

G-2 blocks this receipt, and the missing independent approval is the only thing it blocks on. approved_by is deliberately null: INFRA cannot record its own review, and no other seat has reviewed this revision. Ove's GO authorised the self-hosted bypass as a decision, which is not the same as a review of this diff, so it is recorded in 'task' and not laundered into approved_by. QUALITY (or Ove) stamping approved_by is what turns the gate green; nothing else in the receipt has to change.

unverified: No GitHub Actions run has executed on the self-hosted runner from this change. The workflows were not dispatched from this container, so the runner picking up a job, checking out, and completing a gate step was never observed.

The srv1778002 runner's online state and label set were not inspected. If it does not carry all three of self-hosted, Linux and X64, these jobs queue indefinitely rather than failing loudly — which looks like a pending required check, not an error. Confirm the labels on the runner before treating the gates as restored.

actions/setup-python@v5 was not exercised on the VPS runner. On a GitHub-hosted image it resolves Python 3.12 from the pre-seeded tool cache; a self-hosted runner without that cache downloads and builds it, which needs build tooling and outbound network on the VPS. If it is missing, the gates fail at the setup-python step rather than at a gate.

pip install pyyaml and pip install pyyaml pytest run against whatever Python environment the VPS runner exposes, which was not inspected. A system Python marked externally-managed would reject the plain pip install used by the unchanged step bodies.

Runner hygiene was not assessed. A self-hosted runner reuses its filesystem between jobs, unlike an ephemeral hosted VM, so state left by one pull request can leak into the next. Nothing in this change isolates the workspace.

The security posture of running pull-request workflows on a persistent org runner was not analysed here. These workflows check out the pull request head and pip install on that runner. For a private repository with only trusted bots that is the accepted trade for having gates at all, but it is a real change in blast radius from an ephemeral hosted VM and it is Ove's call, not INFRA's.

The open pull requests #29 and #30 were not modified. GitHub Actions reads workflow files from the pull request head for pull_request events, so those two still request ubuntu-latest and keep failing on the spending limit until this change reaches their heads, either by merging main into them or by merging this pull request first and rebasing.

No independent review of this revision has happened, so approved_by is null and G-2 fails on this receipt (command 7). This follows .receipts/bot-05-infrastructure/claude-mcp-json-hindsight-20260930T023348Z-239b2b18.json, which left the field empty after greptile P1 4140306040 called a named-but-absent reviewer a recorded approval that never happened.

rollback_plan: Restore ubuntu-latest in all five jobs: run git revert on this change's commit, or edit the three workflow files back to 'runs-on: ubuntu-latest' in .github/workflows/gates.yml (gates, gate-self-test), .github/workflows/gates-template-sync.yml (sync) and ci/.github/workflows/gates.yml (gates, gate-self-test), keeping the live and template bodies identical. Recovery is the next workflow trigger, so seconds after the push — GitHub Actions reads runs-on fresh per run and holds no state. No data implications: nothing is deployed, no migration and no cache is involved, and the only effect of reverting is that gate jobs go back to the GitHub-hosted queue, where the spending limit fails them in about 3 seconds.
